deploy-bot: Started staged rollout 'pilot-slice-v2' -> 12% traffic to pilot pool (us-west-2) :arrow_forward:

Sam: Observability alert — 503 rate up on /v1/generate in us-west-2 since 12:02 (sudden jump from 0.8% to 6.9%). Paging SRE oncall. :rotating_light:

Laura: Seeing same in traces — majority of 503s are gateway responses, not model hosts. Latency also up ~200ms p95.

Jon: Customer support - multiple customers reporting failed generations and billing anomalies (billing increments but no tokens returned). Ticket IDs sent to support queue.

Maya: I'm checking the rollout config now. Quick thought: yesterday's traffic-split object had a new label field. Could be mis-encoded.

Sam: Metric quick link: https://ops.redwood/alerts/alert-181888 (logs + heatmap).

Laura: Logs show proxy returning 5xx with body: `{"code":"backend_unreachable","detail":"no route for tag 'pilotSlice'"}` — hmm tag mismatch.

Maya: Confirmed in k8s config: traffic.bucket label was set to "pilotSlice" in the deployment manifest instead of the canonical "pilot-slice-v2". That's the rollout automation mismatch.

Jon: That explains customer repros. How do we want to proceed — rollback or quick remap?

Sam: Propose immediate traffic cutoff for the pilot slice, then a config patch to fix the label. Rollback command usually: `kubectl -n infra apply -f rollout/block-pilot-traffic.yaml` — but ops automation also supports `rdctl rollout abort pilot-slice-v2`. Which is safest?

Maya: Use rdctl abort to let the console handle graceful draining: `rdctl rollout abort --name=pilot-slice-v2 --reason="503 spike"`

Laura: Adding quick mitigation: add an explicit routing rule that falls back to primary instead of returning 503 for unmatched tags. Patch snippet in case we need hotfix:
```json
{
  "routing": {
    "on_mismatch": "fallback_primary",
    "fallback_priority": ["primary", "secondary"]
  }
}
```

Jon: Support will notify affected customers and pause billing adjustments until we confirm requests are retried. :white_check_mark:

Sam: I'm running the abort now. rdctl output: `Started abort for pilot-slice-v2 (id: rr-8791). Draining 12% traffic -> 0%`

deploy-bot: Rollout aborted by Sam at 12:09. New active weights: pilot-slice-v2=0, primary=100.

Laura: Post-abort quick check: 503 rate dropped back to baseline within 30s. p95 latency trending down.

Maya: I'll open a patch PR to make the label validation stricter in automation and add a CI check. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4821 — includes schema validation for traffic.bucket values.

Sam: Please also add an observability alert to detect tag-mismatch errors specifically (`backend_unreachable` + "no route for tag"). That would've caught it earlier.

Jon: Support note drafted and sent. Will follow-up with affected customers when PR merged and new rollout reattempted.

Laura: Postmortem follow-ups: 1) stricter label schema, 2) pre-rollout dry-run that verifies routing table entries, 3) automated rollback-on-503-threshold option for staged rollouts.

Maya: I'll own the PR and the dry-run task. Assigning follow-ups in JIRA (RD-1253, RD-1254, RD-1255).

Sam: Thanks everyone. Ticket will be closed when PR merges and we successfully re-roll with the corrected label. :thumbsup:

Jon: Customer impact summary: ~0.6% of requests in the window failed; billing hold applied; outreach scheduled.

deploy-bot: Incident resolved (status: mitigated) — follow-ups assigned.
